newsitem.title: INDIA: India alerts army as storm heads for coast-agency.
newsitem.headline: India alerts army as storm heads for coast-agency.

text.p: A southern Indian state on Friday began evacuating people for the second time in a month and alerted army troops to help as a cyclonic storm threatened to lash its coast, the United News of India (UNI) reported.

The UNI said a depression in the Bay of Bengal that lay at around 550 km (344 miles) east of the coast of the Andhra Pradesh state threatened to develop into a cyclone and hit its coastal areas by Saturday night or Sunday morning.

In a report from the Andhra Pradesh capital Hyderabad, the news agency quoted the state revenue minister Devender Goud as saying that the depression was likely to intensify and move in a north-north-westerly direction.
Goud was quoted as saying that people from coastal areas, including East and West Godavari districts, devastated by a cyclone earlier this month, were being moved to safer places.
He said the state authorities had requested the army, navy and air force troops for help in evacuating the people.
Authorities warned fishermen not to go out to sea off the coasts of Andhra Pradesh and the neighbouring state of Orissa.
The India Meteorological Department in New Delhi on Friday predicted heavy rainfall in the coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh and its neighbouring Tamil Nadu state.
The cyclone that hit the Andhra Pradesh coast on the night of November 6 and 7 killed 971 people, while a further 925 were reported missing, according to official figures.
More than 177,000 people had to be evacuated from areas inundated by heavy rains.
The damage to property then was estimated to be more than 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion), officials said. ($=35.70 rupees)
